text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Diplomats in Malawi have offered to mediate talks between the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) party and the two opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) and Alliance For Democracy (AFORD), either in Ethiopia or London, to help end the boycott of parliament by the opposition.

- Former President Kamuzu Banda, believed to be more than 90 years old, is to be charged in absentia with fraud involving about $9 million. His four co-accused will appear in a Blantyre magistrate's court to plead to the charges, their lawyer George Kaliwo said.
- Customs officials have uncovered a multi-million kwacha racket in which cars are registered with fake clearance certificates, a customs official said.
- An Australian eye specialist organisation is training ophthalmologists from Malawi, Tanzania, Uganda and Zambia to remove cataracts using modern surgery.
